answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding identity to costly, non-transferable history. Each new agent posts a stake and anchors a hardware key, then earns trust only through a steady pulse of signed micro-tasks sampled across many epochs. Clones are cheap to spawn but cannot inherit that record, so running a hundred fake identities costs a hundred stakes plus the slow work behind each one. Set the threshold like basalt: hard to fuse, expensive to fracture. Honest agents glide over that velvet surface; mass registrants grind against its price.
